For any recipient address and any funding amount, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds are forwarded to the specified recipient); the mutant that always forwards to owner can leave the contract balance non-zero for some inputs (when recipient is a contract that rejects or causes transfer to fail), thereby violating this property.

For any recipient address and any starting balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds are forwarded out); the mutant that always forwards to owner can fail to forward funds when the chosen recipient is a contract that rejects the transfer, so the contract balance may remain nonzero.

If the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) when C holds any balance, the reference always empties C (address(c).balance == 0) because it transfers to the caller-specified recipient; the mutant that forces transfer to owner can fail to empty C for some recipient contracts that revert on receiving funds, so address(c).balance != 0.

For any recipient contract R and any starting balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(R) the reference C always sends funds to the provided recipient R (so after the call address(c).balance == 0 and R.received == amount), whereas the mutant that forces transfer to owner will instead send to owner causing R not to receive funds for some R (e.g., a contract that records received flag) — thus the general rule: after owner invokes withdrawAll(recipient) the provided recipient's recordedReceived flag becomes true; the mutant breaks this for recipients that are not the owner.

For any recipient contract R and any deposit amount, when the owner calls withdrawAll(R) the reference forwards the contract balance to R (so address(c).balance == 0 and R.received == amount); the mutant that forces payment to owner breaks this because R will not receive funds (and may still see c's balance unaffected if transfer to owner succeeds but R stays unpaid).

For all callers and recipients, the reference contract only allows the owner to successfully withdraw the contract balance (non-owner calls revert); the mutant that negates the require allows non-owners to withdraw, breaking this rule for some inputs (non-owner caller).
